transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I guess… I’m here because I can’t stop noticing this sagging, uneven part around my jaw and neck. People say it looks normal, but it doesn’t to me. I feel like it’s the first thing people see—families I work with, nurses, people at church… everyone.
Do you feel that this unevenness around your jaw and neck is making you look physically unattractive or deformed in some way?

Yes… I do. I know people tell me it looks normal, but to me it looks saggy and uneven, like it stands out right away. I feel like families I work with, nurses, people at church… they notice it when they look at me.
How much does this concern about your jaw and neck bother you or affect your daily life?

It… it does get in the way. I don’t really like saying that, but I’ve passed up helping lead meetings or doing more supervisory things because I’m worried everyone will be looking at my face and neck.

And sometimes I get stuck trying to make myself look okay before work, then I fall behind on paperwork. I’ve also stopped going to some book club and walking club things… getting ready just feels like too much.
Have you noticed any other parts of your body that also seem uneven or unattractive to you, or is your main concern specifically with your jaw and neck?
It’s mostly the jaw and neck. That sagging, uneven spot… I just can’t stop seeing it. Even when people say it looks normal, I feel like it’s what families, nurses, or people at church notice first.
